## ⛔ CORRECTION — this card's central premise was wrong, and it was mine

Posted before any decision is taken on it. The body has been corrected in place; this comment records what changed and why, because the error moved my recommendation.

**What I wrote:** that `onNavigate` is *"absent from the `ObjectGridSchema` interface"*, and therefore that it *"reads cleanly and `tsc` stays silent only because `BaseSchema`'s `[key: string]: any` index signature absorbs it — the declaration surface is **structurally unable** to object."*

**What is true**, verified by me on `origin/main` just now:

```
packages/types/src/objectql.ts:847      onNavigate?: (recordId: string | number, action?: string) => void;
```

`ObjectGridSchema` spans lines **532–888**, and `onNavigate` is an **explicitly declared member at :847, with its own doc comment** (*"Callback for page-level navigation (used by 'page' mode). Called with recordId and action"*). Nothing is being absorbed by an index signature.

**Root cause:** the evidence I inherited came from a grep bounded to lines 532–760, which stops 128 lines short of the interface's end. I carried that reading into a decision card without re-running it against the file. Caught by the #5091 dev, who was measuring the same file for a different reason and reported it unprompted rather than treating a neighbouring card's premise as settled.

### What this changes

**The "structurally unable to object" argument is withdrawn entirely.** The type declares this key on purpose and documents what it is for. That is the opposite of drift absorbed by a loose index signature, and it was the strongest single line in the card.

**Option A is now materially more expensive than I priced it.** I called moving `onNavigate` off the schema read point *"cheap"*. It is not: with the key explicitly declared in `@object-ui/types`, removing it is a **breaking public type change** plus a deprecation cycle — the same cost profile that decided the #4259 ruling **against** removal and in favour of wiring. My recommendation of A was built on the belief that nothing declared it. **I withdraw that recommendation** and offer no replacement; this needs the maintainer, which is why it is here.

**The "single breach in an otherwise clean line" framing is weakened.** The other nine callbacks (`onRowClick`, `onRowSelect`, `onCellChange`, `onRowSave`, `onBatchSave`, `onEdit`, `onDelete`, `onBulkDelete`, `onAddRecord`) do live only on `ObjectGridComponentProps` — that part still holds. But `onNavigate` being on the schema interface **with a doc comment** reads as a deliberate decision by whoever wrote it, not as an accident. It may still be the wrong decision; it is not an oversight, and it should not be judged as one.

### What survives, unchanged

- It is **absent from `GRID_QUERY_INPUTS`**, so the manifest, the designer panel and the generated `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts` still deny a key the renderer reads at `ObjectGrid.tsx:1187`. That is the original defect and it is intact.
- It is a **function value**, and a schema is a serialisable document — so it cannot survive a metadata round-trip regardless of what declares it. This is now the card's strongest remaining argument, and it is untouched by the correction.
- The documentation consequence is unchanged: the README/docs claim *"the grid never reads a callback off the schema"* was narrowed to *"never reads any of these nine"* because of this key.

### The pattern, for the record

Three times today I have taken a document's word for the repository's state — a transferred card (#5217, already fixed), a maintainer ruling's premise (#5091's `bulkActionDefs` symmetry), and now a grep range I did not re-run. All three were caught by someone measuring rather than reading. **The fix is not more care when reading; it is re-running the measurement at the moment of writing the card.** Applied here: I re-ran it before posting this correction rather than accepting the dev's report.

## 裁决 — maintainer RULED this. ⛔ Do not re-open it.

⚠️ The card is titled `[Decision]`, but the decision was made. Maintainer ruling recorded 2026-08-19 (27-card decision-inbox review, verbatim reply 「全部接受」):

> **Ruling: Option C — keep `onNavigate` as an explicit, documented exception.**
> - **Exemption comment at the read site** (`ObjectGrid.tsx` schema read), following the pattern **PR #5241** established for the other non-author keys; **extend `gridNonAuthorKeys.test.tsx`** accordingly.
> - The `@object-ui/types` declaration (`objectql.ts:847`) gains a **programmatic-only note**: the key is a **function value, inexpressible in JSON/YAML metadata** — authors cannot use it; programmatic callers should prefer `ObjectGridComponentProps` like its nine siblings.
> - The docs sentence stays narrowed accordingly.
> - ⛔ **Why not A (remove):** with the key explicitly declared, removal is a breaking public type change plus a deprecation cycle — for **zero measured harm**, in the launch window, that price fails scope discipline. A may be re-evaluated at the next major.
> - ⛔ **Why not B (declare in `GRID_QUERY_INPUTS`):** it would publish to the designer a key **no author can ever express** — the most AI-error-prone option.

⛔ Do not remove the key. ⛔ Do not add it to `GRID_QUERY_INPUTS`. The execution is **zero behaviour change**.

## ⚠️ Read the card's own CORRECTION comment before you read its body

This card carries a **self-correction from its author** that withdrew its central premise, and the body was edited in place. The withdrawn claim was that `onNavigate` is *absent* from `ObjectGridSchema` and only survives because `BaseSchema`'s `[key: string]: any` absorbs it. **That is false.** It is an **explicitly declared member at `objectql.ts:847` with its own doc comment**. The bad evidence came from a grep bounded to lines 532–760, which stops 128 lines short of the interface's end (it spans 532–888).

⇒ ⛔ **Do not describe this key as drift, as an oversight, or as absorbed by an index signature.** It was declared on purpose and documented. It may still be the wrong decision — it is **not an accident**, and the ruling turns on exactly that distinction.

✅ What survives the correction, and is what you are documenting:
- It is **absent from `GRID_QUERY_INPUTS`**, so the manifest, the designer panel and the generated `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts` deny a key the renderer reads at `ObjectGrid.tsx:1187`.
- ⭐ **It is a function value, and a schema is a serialisable document** — so it cannot survive a metadata round-trip **regardless of what declares it**. The correction calls this the card's strongest remaining argument. ✅ That is the sentence your type note should carry.
- The nine siblings (`onRowClick`, `onRowSelect`, `onCellChange`, `onRowSave`, `onBatchSave`, `onEdit`, `onDelete`, `onBulkDelete`, `onAddRecord`) **do** live only on `ObjectGridComponentProps`.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not inherit

1. ⛔ **Re-run every line number.** `objectql.ts:847`, `ObjectGrid.tsx:1187`, the 532–888 span — all measured on 2026-08-18/19, and both files have moved since (`packages/types` took five PRs today; `ObjectGrid.tsx` has #6109 landing). ⚠️ **This card's own history is the argument**: it went wrong precisely by carrying a stale grep range into a decision. ✅ Re-derive each site and report what you found.
2. ⚠️ **Find PR #5241's pattern and follow it — ⛔ do not invent an exemption format.** The ruling says "following the pattern PR #5241 established for the other non-author keys". ✅ Quote the shape you found and mirror it. If the pattern has since changed, say so.
3. ⚠️ **`gridNonAuthorKeys.test.tsx` must be EXTENDED, not rewritten.** It already pins the other non-author keys. ⛔ Adding `onNavigate` must not weaken what it asserts about the nine — ✅ state the before/after count and confirm the nine still fail if their exemption is removed.
4. ⚠️ **The docs sentence was already narrowed** from *"the grid never reads a callback off the schema"* to *"never reads any of these nine"* — **because of this key**. ✅ Verify the current wording before editing; if it is already correct, say so and leave it. ⛔ Do not re-narrow a sentence that is already narrow.

## Verification

⚠️ **This is a zero-behaviour-change card, so an ordinary behavioural ablation has nothing to show** — the same shape as #5876 today. ✅ The pin is on the **exemption ledger**: removing `onNavigate`'s exemption entry must turn `gridNonAuthorKeys.test.tsx` **red**, and the nine siblings' entries must each still be individually load-bearing. ⚠️ ⛔ State explicitly **which of your assertions would still pass if your change were reverted** — and if the honest answer is "all of them", the test is not pinning this card and must be re-aimed.

⚠️ **Five phantom-class defects were self-caught by devs on this round's cards**, all one root: *an assertion or control that cannot distinguish the two states of the world.* Make each control a string present in **both** versions of the file. ⚠️ **Commit before you ablate** — and note the sharper variant measured on #5674: **`git checkout <ref> -- <path>` writes the INDEX as well as the worktree**, so reading a baseline that way and restoring with `git checkout -- <path>` restores *the baseline over your work*.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping injected **and separately** removed text; ⚠️ print the landing site; ⚠️ assert anchor uniqueness before writing; ⚠️ restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a cwd-independent command; confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` is empty afterwards.

**Gates by name, with exit codes:** `type-check` for `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/plugin-grid` (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name; distinguish the **unbuilt-closure** red from the **missing-`node_modules`** red; ⚠️ **build `./examples/**` too**), root-form vitest quoting per-test names, the downstream **prefix-form** sweep with the direction **demonstrated**, eslint with merge-base delta (⚠️ plain `eslint .`; ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`), and the doc gates if you touch the docs sentence.

⚠️ **Use `pnpm exec vitest run [paths]` from the repo root** — ⛔ **not** `pnpm --filter … test -- [paths]`. ⚠️ **Zero-match pnpm trap**: a filter matching nothing prints *"No projects matched the filters"* and exits **0**. ⚠️ **A cached turbo green is not a measurement** — use `--force` on any turbo gate you treat as evidence. Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing (⚠️ **#6073 widened it beyond `/src/`** today); a comments-and-docs change may legitimately owe nothing, and empty frontmatter is this repo's explicit "releases nothing" declaration. ⚠️ **Standing rule from #5874:** derive your gate set by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**.

## Deliverable

Draft PR, body with `Fixes #5234`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge — the PM lands it. ⚠️ **Audit your PR body for closing keywords near any sibling issue number — GitHub's parser ignores negation** (measured on #5674 today). Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose) and return it. State, per gate: command, exit code, what a red would have meant; every re-derived line number against the one the card gives; PR #5241's pattern as you found it; the before/after assertion count in `gridNonAuthorKeys.test.tsx`; **which of your assertions would still pass on a revert**; and any deviation with its reason.

## ⚠️ First, a relaunch-note correction — the earlier run did NOT leave nothing behind

## PR #5241's pattern, as found

Four elements at a read site: the verdict phrased "deliberately absent from `GRID_QUERY_INPUTS`"; the ruling (maintainer, date, issue); **who writes the key**, as `file:line`; the contract's own verdict plus a pointer to the test. Read back off `main`, `columnState` (`:610`) and `hideRowHeightToggle` (`:3509`) carry exactly that, closing on "Both halves — unlisted here, rejected there — are pinned by `__tests__/gridNonAuthorKeys.test.tsx` … so this exemption cannot decay into a silent drop." The landed comment mirrors that shape, including that closing sentence.

**One element adapted, deliberately:** element 3 wants a producer `file:line`, and this key has none — *nobody writes it*, which is the ruling. The comment carries the honest analogue (function value, no document can hold it, programmatic callers use `ObjectGridComponentProps`) instead of inventing a citation. The pattern has not otherwise changed since #5241.

- `packages/plugin-grid/README.md:516` — **still the un-narrowed universal**, "never reads a callback off the schema". That is the claim this key falsifies, and it was still live. Narrowed.

**31 → 41 cases; 36 → 57 `expect(` calls; +264 / −0 lines.** Counts from `vitest list`, not from reading the file. The only edit outside the appended block is three added `node:` imports — every pre-existing assertion is byte-identical.

**Which assertions would still pass on a revert — 7 of the 10.** Not-published (×2 tags), spec-rejects-by-name, parser `unknown-prop`, the type still declares it, the nine siblings still props-only, the renderer still reads it: all were true before this card. They are the ledger's premises, kept so the exemption cannot decay, but alone they would pin nothing. **Three cases distinguish the two states** and are the deliverable: the read site carries the exemption comment; the declaration carries the programmatic-only note; and the four #5091 exemptions are still present (the control that stops the first two passing vacuously). Since the ruling's deliverable is prose, those three read the source — the way `ObjectGrid.exportOptionsKeys.test.ts` in the same directory already does — each anchored on text present in **both** states, so a red means the comment went missing, never that the anchor moved.

### Ablations — four legs, predicted before running, all matched

Committed first. Each: anchor uniqueness asserted before writing, landing site printed, mutation proved on disk by grepping the **removed** text *and* a separately **injected** marker, restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths, `git diff HEAD --stat` empty after.

Same finding #5241 recorded. Separately, `@object-ui/types` **was** rebuilt before the plugin-grid type-check so that green is over rebuilt `dist/*.d.ts`.

**Direction demonstrated:** prefix `'...@object-ui/types'` → **43** packages (downstream consumers); suffix `'@object-ui/types...'` → **1** (upstream deps; types has none). Opposite directions; the prefix form is the one swept.
